title: Diagnose (AI)
subtitle: One-tap health check of your car
notConnected: Not connected. Pair your adapter on the Connect tab (or switch to the Simulator in Settings) to run a diagnosis.
intro: Describe what’s wrong and tap “Investigate”, or tap “Check everything” to read your car’s fault codes, readiness and live data and get a plain-language health report.

clear.title: Clear fault codes?
clear.body: This erases stored/pending codes and resets readiness monitors. Codes will return if the fault persists.

focus.title: Focused on fault code {{code}}
focus.help: The report explains this code first: what it means, likely causes and what to check.

followUp.title: Ask about this report
followUp.needsProvider: Follow-up questions need an AI provider. This report came from the on-device rules; set up a provider in Settings → AI assistant and re-run the diagnosis.
followUp.placeholder: Ask a question about this report

driver.start_engine_idle: Start the engine and let it idle.
driver.engine_off_ignition_on: Switch the engine off and leave the ignition on.
driver.restart_engine: Switch the engine off, then start it again.
driver.hold_2500_rpm: In Park or Neutral, hold the engine at 2500 rpm for 10 seconds.
driver.electrical_load_on: Switch on the headlights, the A/C and the rear demister.
driver.electrical_load_off: Switch the headlights, the A/C and the rear demister off.
driver.wiggle_connector: With the engine idling, gently flex the wiring and connector of the sensor the app is watching for 10 seconds.
driver.smoke_colour: With the engine running, look at the exhaust: what colour is the smoke?

good.title: Battery and starting look good
good.detail: Resting {{resting}} V, cranking dip {{dip}} V, charging {{charging}} V. The battery holds its voltage well while the engine cranks.

fair.title: Battery is fair
fair.detail: Resting {{resting}} V, cranking dip {{dip}} V, charging {{charging}} V. The voltage dips a little low while cranking, so the battery is ageing; have it tested before winter.

weak.title: Battery is weak
weak.detail: Resting {{resting}} V, cranking dip {{dip}} V, charging {{charging}} V. The voltage drops too far while cranking; have the battery tested and replace it if it fails.

unknown.title: Battery check incomplete
unknown.detail: Resting {{resting}} V, cranking dip {{dip}} V, charging {{charging}} V. The engine restart was not captured, so the battery condition could not be judged.

ok.title: Fuel trims are normal
ok.detail: Total fuel trim {{idle}} % at idle, within ±10 %: the engine control is not correcting for a mixture fault.

lean.title: Engine runs lean at idle
lean.detail: Total fuel trim {{idle}} % at idle: the engine control adds fuel to make up for extra air or too little fuel. Look for a vacuum leak, a dirty MAF sensor or weak fuel delivery.

rich.title: Engine runs rich
rich.detail: The total fuel trim is -10 % or lower (at idle: {{idle}} %): the engine control removes fuel. Check for leaking injectors, high fuel pressure, a sticking purge valve or a faulty oxygen or coolant sensor.

vacuum_leak.title: Likely vacuum leak
vacuum_leak.detail: Total fuel trim {{idle}} % at idle improves to {{hold}} % at 2500 rpm: extra air that matters most at idle. Check the intake hoses, the brake-servo hose, the crankcase ventilation and the intake gasket.

lean_all_speeds.title: Engine runs lean at all speeds
lean_all_speeds.detail: Total fuel trim {{idle}} % at idle and still {{hold}} % at 2500 rpm: more likely the MAF sensor or the fuel supply (pump, filter, injectors) than a vacuum leak.

ok.title: Boost pressure looks normal
ok.detail: {{idle}} kPa over atmospheric pressure at idle, within the expected range for this car (and the rev hold too, when it was done).

idle_high.title: Boost slightly high at idle
idle_high.detail: {{idle}} kPa over atmospheric pressure at idle is above the expected range, but not enough to suggest stuck turbo vanes. Recheck if power problems appear.

stuck_vnt.title: Turbo vanes may be stuck
stuck_vnt.detail: {{idle}} kPa over atmospheric pressure at idle: a variable-vane turbo stuck closed builds boost where there should be almost none. Have the turbo vanes and their actuator checked.

map_below_baro.title: Manifold pressure reading implausible
map_below_baro.detail: The intake manifold pressure reads {{idle}} kPa against atmospheric pressure at idle, which a diesel cannot do. Check the MAP sensor and its wiring before judging the turbo.

no_boost_hold.title: Little or no boost at 2500 rpm
no_boost_hold.detail: Only {{hold}} kPa over atmospheric pressure during the rev hold ({{rpm}} rpm), below the expected range. Look for a boost leak (intercooler hoses, clamps), sticking turbo vanes or a vacuum supply fault.

overboost_hold.title: Boost too high at 2500 rpm
overboost_hold.detail: {{hold}} kPa over atmospheric pressure during the rev hold ({{rpm}} rpm), above the expected range: overboost, often turbo vanes sticking closed or their control valve.

stuck_sensor.title: Manifold pressure sensor looks stuck
stuck_sensor.detail: The manifold pressure barely changed while the engine went from idle to {{rpm}} rpm. Check the MAP sensor before judging the boost.

hold_not_reached.title: Rev hold not reached
hold_not_reached.detail: The engine reached only {{rpm}} rpm during the rev hold, so boost at speed was not judged. Only the idle part ({{idle}} kPa over atmospheric pressure) was checked.

ok.title: Alternator keeps up under load
ok.detail: {{volts}} V at {{rpm}} rpm with the headlights, A/C and rear demister on: the alternator charges well under load.

weakUnderLoad.title: Charging weak under load
weakUnderLoad.detail: Only {{volts}} V at {{rpm}} rpm with the headlights, A/C and rear demister on (expected 13.2 V or more). Have the alternator, its belt and the battery connections checked.

ok.title: Cooling looks normal
ok.detail: Coolant {{now}} °C now; the latest cold start warmed up normally (peak {{max}} °C).

hot_now.title: Engine running hot
hot_now.detail: Coolant {{now}} °C now, at or above 105 °C. Check the coolant level (only with the engine cold), the radiator fan and the thermostat.

overheat_now.title: Engine overheating
overheat_now.detail: Coolant {{now}} °C now, at or above 115 °C. Stop the engine as soon as it is safe and let it cool; do not open the coolant cap while hot.

thermostat_open.title: Thermostat may be stuck open
thermostat_open.detail: On the latest cold start the coolant peaked at only {{max}} °C after {{driven}} min of driving. A thermostat stuck open keeps the engine too cold: more fuel, a weak heater and more wear.

slow_warmup.title: Engine warms up slowly
slow_warmup.detail: On the latest cold start the coolant took {{warmup}} min to reach 80 °C. The thermostat may be opening too early; recheck after a few more cold starts.

trip_overheat.title: Engine got hot on a recent drive
trip_overheat.detail: A recorded drive reached {{max}} °C. Check the coolant level, the radiator fan and the water pump.

no_cold_trip.title: Warm-up not checked
no_cold_trip.detail: No recorded drive started from a cold engine, so only the current coolant temperature ({{now}} °C) was checked. Record the next cold start to check the warm-up.

none.title: No significant misfires
none.detail: The misfire monitors counted {{total}} misfires in total: nothing that points to a fault.

cylinder.title: Misfires on cylinder {{cylinder}}
cylinder.detail: Cylinder {{cylinder}} misfired {{count}} times, far more than the others. Check its spark plug, ignition coil and injector (swapping the coil with a neighbour shows whether the misfire follows).

random.title: Misfires on several cylinders
random.detail: {{total}} misfires spread across the cylinders: a shared cause is more likely, such as a vacuum leak, low fuel pressure, worn spark plugs or the EGR.

start.title: What's wrong?
start.inputA11y: Describe what's wrong with the car

agent.uncitedDropped_one: {{count}} finding the AI did not back with a step of this run was left out.
agent.uncitedDropped_other: {{count}} findings the AI did not back with a step of this run were left out.
